seoTitle: How to Save Email Attachments to SharePoint With Power Automate
metaDescription: Automatically save Outlook email attachments to a SharePoint document library with Power Automate — the trigger settings that matter, and why Create file fails without them.
intro: Manually pulling attachments out of email and dropping them into SharePoint is a small chore that quietly eats a chunk of every week. Power Automate replaces it with a flow that watches your inbox and saves matching attachments the moment they arrive. This guide follows a real flow built around a "When a new email arrives (V3)" trigger filtered to a specific subject line, so you can see the actual trigger configuration and the inbox it's watching, not just a description of the steps.
prerequisites: A Microsoft 365 account with access to Power Automate and the target SharePoint site
Edit access to the document library the flow will write to
costNote: Outlook and SharePoint are both standard connectors, so this flow runs on the Power Automate allowance included with most Microsoft 365 plans. No premium Power Automate license is needed unless you later add a premium connector.

steps.heading: Find your existing flows or start a new one
steps.body: Open My flows in Power Automate to see everything you've already built, listed by Name, Modified date, and Type. Name flows clearly as this list grows — entries like "Automated Report" or "When a new email arrives (V3) -> Condition Apply to e..." describe what they do at a glance, which matters once you have a dozen of them. To start fresh, use New flow and choose Automated cloud flow, since this needs to fire on an event (a new email) instead of a fixed schedule.

image.caption: The My flows list, showing existing automated flows including one built around a new-email trigger with a condition step.

steps.heading: Configure the When a new email arrives trigger
steps.body: The trigger block, "When a new email arrives (V3)," connects to your Outlook mailbox. Open its Advanced parameters and set Include Attachments to Yes, which makes the attachment bytes available to later steps, and Subject Filter to a value like "Automated Reports," which narrows the trigger to matching emails only. Set Only with Attachments to Yes alongside them so the flow doesn't fire at all on messages with nothing to save. Skipping Include Attachments is the most common reason Create file fails later with a null-content error.

image.caption: The email trigger's Advanced parameters panel, with Include Attachments set to Yes and a Subject Filter narrowing it to matching emails.

steps.heading: Confirm what the trigger is watching
steps.body: Check the real inbox the flow is connected to before trusting the automation. In this account, the Outlook inbox shows a thread of test emails with the subject "Automated Report," sent to confirm the trigger fires as expected. Sending yourself one test email with the target subject and an attachment, before turning the flow loose on real mail, is the fastest way to catch a misconfigured filter.

image.caption: The connected Outlook inbox with a series of "Automated Report" test emails, used to confirm the trigger's subject filter is matching correctly.

steps.heading: Save each attachment to a SharePoint document library
steps.body: Add a "Create file" action from the SharePoint connector under the trigger, and point it at your target site and document library. Set File Name to the Attachments Name dynamic value and File Content to Attachments Content. Attachments is a collection, not a single value, so Power Automate wraps the Create file action in an Apply to each loop automatically the moment you pick that dynamic content. A message with three files creates three rows without any extra step. To keep files organized, either add a condition before Create file that checks the sender or subject and branches into a subfolder, or follow up with an "Update file properties" action to tag the new file with sender and received-date metadata instead of moving it into a folder.

steps.heading: Guard against duplicate files
steps.body: Re-sent emails or near-duplicate messages with the same filename can overwrite each other in the library, or just clutter it. Add a check before the Create file step, either a "Get file metadata" call against the target folder or a simple existence check. If a match turns up, append a timestamp or counter to the filename instead of skipping the save, so nothing gets silently lost.

troubleshooting.problem: Create file fails with a 400 Bad Request the first time the flow runs
troubleshooting.cause: Include Attachments was left at its default of No on the trigger, so the attachment's content bytes are null by the time Create file tries to read them.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the trigger's Advanced parameters and set Include Attachments to Yes.

troubleshooting.problem: The flow runs on every email, even ones with nothing to save
troubleshooting.cause: Only with Attachments was left unset on the trigger.
troubleshooting.fix: Set Only with Attachments to Yes in the same Advanced parameters panel.

troubleshooting.problem: A saved file opens as corrupted, or won't open at all
troubleshooting.cause: File Content in the Create file action was mapped to the wrong dynamic value, usually Attachments Name instead of Attachments Content, or an inline signature image got swept in as if it were a real attachment.
troubleshooting.fix: Recheck that File Content points to Attachments Content, and add a condition to skip attachments under a few KB if signature images keep getting saved.

faq.question: Can I filter which emails trigger the flow?
faq.answer: Yes. The trigger's Advanced parameters include Subject Filter, sender and folder options, and Only with Attachments, so the flow only fires on matching mail that has something to save.

faq.question: What happens if an email has multiple attachments?
faq.answer: Power Automate wraps the Create file action in an Apply to each loop automatically the moment you map its File Content field to the Attachments Content dynamic value. There's no separate loop to build by hand.

faq.question: How do I avoid saving duplicate files?
faq.answer: Add a file-existence check against the target SharePoint folder before the Create file step, and append a timestamp or counter to the filename if a match is found.

faq.question: Can attachments be organized or tagged automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, two ways: a condition on sender or subject before Create file to route files into different folders, or an Update file properties step afterward to tag the file with metadata like sender and received date instead of moving it.

faq.question: Do I need Include Attachments turned on for this to work?
faq.answer: Yes. Without it, the attachment content bytes are null and the Create file action fails. Only with Attachments is a separate, optional setting that just stops the flow firing on mail with no attachments at all.
